title: Burns to Face and Buttocks
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} is a child presenting with burns in concerning patterns: immersion burns on buttocks (stocking-glove distribution with sharp demarcation), cigarette burns (circular punched-out lesions), burns on face inappropriate for developmental stage. History is inconsistent with the injury pattern, and there was a delay in seeking care. Red flags for non-accidental trauma: injury inconsistent with history, delay in presentation, concerning burn patterns (immersion, cigarette, stocking-glove), injuries in various stages of healing, and concerning caregiver affect. Management: full skeletal survey (look for other fractures in various healing stages), head CT (rule out abusive head trauma), ophthalmology exam (retinal hemorrhages). Document all injuries thoroughly with photographs. Admit for safety. Report to Child Protective Services (mandatory reporting). Social work and child protection team consultation.
chief_complaint: Burns in concerning patterns, inconsistent history
